method: Read every source, candidate and reference pairing. Inspect all distinct quoted formulations for numbers, negation, symptom attribution, count scope, rating context, timing and medication relation.
Independently compare all emitted candidate fields with source-supported reference claims, including candidates beyond the evaluator checks.

Compare each normalized observation with its reference by symptom, including all nine core fields and issue sets. There is at most one normalized observation per symptom in each report of this dataset.
Check all raw and normalized quotes as literal source substrings; verify that every candidate quote is retained in the corresponding normalized evidence set.
Confirm stored candidates equal parsed raw_response candidates. No normalizer, extractor, model call, correction replay or prediction edit was performed for this audit.
scope: Known synthetic longitudinal integration; findings apply to this frozen run and are not a general model accuracy claim.
verdict: No semantic extraction or normalized core-field error found in these 71 reports. Predictions are suitable for the authorized integration demo without an evidence exception or rerun.

provenance.hash_definition: SHA-256 of exact file bytes; canonical dataset hashes below are separately copied from the frozen protocol.

unchanged_evaluator_results.interpretation: Passing candidate checks confirms expected claims were found. It does not by itself establish exact raw candidate count or grouping; the extra supported TXT-R002 candidate is disclosed separately.

quotes: I have not vomited at all today.
I haven't vomited so far today.
findings.explanation: The original narrative and verbalized form each state zero vomiting for the same reporting interval. The model emitted one candidate per statement instead of one distinct agreeing claim. Both candidates correctly contain absent, count 0 and day_to_date.
findings.normalization_result: One vomiting observation with count 0 and both source quotes. The two conflicting nausea ratings, 2/5 and 3/5, remain represented by null severity and a conflicting_sources issue.

findings.explanation: Both phrases appear in the two supporting nausea statements and identify the same day-to-submission interval. The date and the source conflict are preserved.

findings.quote: I've vomited 2 times so far today, and my vomiting is worst at 2/5 today so far.
findings.explanation: Both phrases occur in the same quote and describe the same reporting interval. Count 2, day_to_date, worst-today severity 2/5 and the date all match.

limitations: This is integration coverage from known synthetic longitudinal data, not a new held-out or clinical validation benchmark. Original starter reports and seed facts were previously used during development.
The 63 generated supplements contain 37 unique raw texts and 26 repeats. Controlled, repetitive wording reduces linguistic difficulty and does not represent unrestricted patient narratives.
Text generation and extraction used the same pinned model, gpt-5.4-mini-2026-03-17. The shared model family and synthetic generation process limit independence and generalization claims.
One unknown-count statement was clarified before extraction and before reference freeze, as disclosed in data/longitudinal_text/editorial_review.json. This review makes no further source changes.

The earlier 20-case run retains its two factual limitations: TH005 omitted the stated day_to_date count scope when the numeric count was unknown; TH012 labeled a morning rating as current. Those errors were not repaired or erased by this integration result.
The extra supported TXT-R002 candidate prevents a claim of exact raw candidate-count agreement on every report. Two literal time_text differences also remain in the unchanged evaluator output.
This audit covers extraction outputs and their references. It does not independently certify the later SQLite aggregation or dashboard rendering.
recommended_action: Use the unchanged predictions for the integration demo; preserve separate semantic, exact wording and raw grouping results. No prompt adjustment, rerun, label edit or source-based evidence exception is indicated by this audit.
